outgoing.name: 19th century
outgoing.excerpt: At the close of the 19th century, the case for atomic theory, that matter was made of particulate objects or atoms, was well established.

outgoing.name: 20th century
outgoing.excerpt: But as the 20th century turned, problems had emerged with this viewpoint.

outgoing.name: Albert Einstein
outgoing.excerpt: In 1905, Albert Einstein provided an explanation of the photoelectric effect, a hitherto troubling experiment which the wave theory of light seemed incapable of explaining.

outgoing.name: Isaac Newton
outgoing.section: Huygens and Newton; earliest theories of light
outgoing.excerpt: However, the theory had difficulties in other matters, and was soon overshadowed by Isaac Newton's corpuscular theory of light.

outgoing.name: Property
outgoing.excerpt: In physics and chemistry, wave-particle duality holds that light and matter exhibit properties of both waves and of particles.

outgoing.name: Rainbow
outgoing.section: Huygens and Newton; earliest theories of light
outgoing.excerpt: With considerably more difficulty, he could also explain refraction through a lens, and the splitting of sunlight into a rainbow by a prism.

outgoing.name: Differential equation
outgoing.excerpt: …or atom, is described by a solution to a differential equation, most typically, the Schroedinger equation.
